hypothesis: EX-stage redirection is being asserted for non-control instructions: ex_redirect fires even though the item in EX is an ALU/ALU-imm/LUI/AUIPC op, so if_stage keeps taking the `redirect` branch and loads PC with the EX ALU result (or a stale/pc+imm value) instead of PC+4. The evidence is that the timeout imem_addr values are literally ALU results: t03_alu_imm parks at 0xfffff804 (a sign-extended ALU/ADDI result), t02_alu_r at 0xfffffffc (= -4), t04_upper at 0x752d9004 (= an LUI immediate << 12), and t01_reset is pinned at 0x8 (a self-referential jump to an ALU result), i.e. PC is being reloaded from the datapath every cycle instead of only on branch/JAL/JALR. Because the same spurious redirect also flushes ID/EX (and, combined with the stall/flush path, clears if_id_valid), no instruction ever retires: x1 never leaves its reset value, no dmem transaction is ever issued, and the ECALL never reaches WB, so halted stays 0 in every suite. The root mechanism is a decode/control defect in which the branch/jump qualifiers feeding ex_redirect (id_ex_jump / id_ex_branch, and hence `taken`) are set or left un-defaulted for ordinary ALU opcodes, and/or the redirect term is not qualified solely by `id_ex_valid && (taken || jal || jalr)`; redirect_pc must be selected only from the branch/JAL target or the masked JALR target.
constraints: Top-level port list/names of rv32i5 and the 8 required module names must not change; imem_addr must remain if_stage.imem_addr and dmem_valid must stay mem_dmem_valid & rst_n & ~halted.
ex_redirect may only be asserted when id_ex_valid=1 AND the instruction is a taken branch or JAL/JALR; no redirection for ALU, ALU-imm, LUI, AUIPC, load/store or ECALL.
redirect_pc for JAL/JALR = (rs1 + imm) & 32'hffff_fffe; for branches = EX pc + imm; never the bare ALU result of a non-control op.
On a taken redirect flush only the two younger items (IF/ID and ID/EX) and set PC to the target; a stall must never clear a valid instruction; PC/IF-ID hold for exactly one cycle on a load-use stall.
